functions.name: immer::for_each_chunk
functions.signature: template <typename Range, typename Fn> void for_each_chunk(const Range& r, Fn&& fn)
functions.description: Low-level traversal helper: calls r.impl().for_each_chunk(fn), applying fn to each contiguous chunk of elements in r. fn is invoked with two pointers delimiting a contiguous block of the container’s value_type. Use when you need efficient block-wise iteration; higher-level algorithms are usually preferred.
requirements: Range must provide r.impl().for_each_chunk(Fn) with the expected callable signature.
Fn must be callable as fn(const value_type*, const value_type*) (pointers delimiting [first,last) for r’s value_type).
r must remain valid for the duration of the call.
Order and coverage of chunks are determined by Range’s implementation.

functions.name: immer::for_each_chunk
functions.signature: template <typename Iterator, typename Fn> void for_each_chunk(const Iterator& first, const Iterator& last, Fn&& fn)
functions.description: Low-level traversal over a subrange [first,last) from an immer container using contiguous internal chunks. fn is invoked with two pointers delimiting each chunk. Internally dispatches to first.impl().for_each_chunk(first.index(), last.index(), fn).
requirements: first and last must originate from the same underlying container implementation; this is debug-checked via assert(&first.impl() == &last.impl()).
The range [first,last) must be valid; first must not go past last.
Iterator must provide impl() and index() compatible with the container’s chunk traversal.
Fn must be callable as fn(const value_type*, const value_type*).
The underlying container must remain valid and unmodified during traversal.

functions.name: immer::for_each_chunk
functions.signature: template <typename T, typename Fn> void for_each_chunk(const T* first, const T* last, Fn&& fn)
functions.description: Primitive pointer overload: invokes fn(first,last) exactly once, treating [first,last) as a single contiguous chunk of T elements.
requirements: first and last must form a valid half-open range [first,last) over T (first and last may be equal; if not, first must be reachable from last by incrementing).
Pointers must be valid for reading T elements in [first,last).
Fn must be callable as fn(const T*, const T*) (accepts the two pointers).

functions.description: Predicate variant of chunk traversal. Iterates contiguous chunks of r, invoking fn on each chunk as fn(first,last). Stops early if fn returns false and returns that boolean; otherwise returns true after all chunks.
requirements: Range must provide r.impl().for_each_chunk_p(Fn) that accepts a callable and returns a bool indicating continuation.
Fn must be callable as fn(const value_type*, const value_type*) and return bool (true to continue, false to stop).
r must remain valid during traversal.

functions.name: immer::diff

functions.description: Computes differences between containers a and b and reports them via differ. Leverages structural sharing of immer containers for near O(|diff|) complexity when b derives from a by a small number of updates. For sets, changed is never called.

requirements: Same container requirements as the Differ overload (a and b must be compatible immer containers with impl().diff available).
If three callables are provided: they must be invocable as added(x), removed(x), changed(x,y).

Callables are decayed and stored in the differ; must be copyable/movable.

import random
import struct
from typing import List

# We generate arbitrary binary data buffers (<=4096 bytes) that are interesting
# for pointer-range traversal: include diverse lengths, patterns, and edge bytes.

_DEF_PATTERNS: List[bytes] = [
    b"",                                   # empty buffer
    b"\x00",                               # single NUL
    b"\xff",                               # single 0xFF
    b"A",                                   # simple ASCII
    b"\x00\xff",                          # two extremes
    bytes(range(256)),                      # 0..255 increasing
    bytes(reversed(range(256))),            # 255..0 decreasing
    (b"ABCD" * 64),                         # repeating short pattern
    (b"\x00" * 1024),                      # long NUL run
    (b"\xff" * 1024),                      # long 0xFF run
]

# Helper to build a structured header that the fuzzer harness can optionally use
# as FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int) for indices/behavior, followed by payload data for
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR. Many harnesses seed multiple FUZZ_PARAM calls from a single
# buffer; we place 3 uint32 values first, then the payload.

def _pack_u32(v: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack("<I", v & 0xFFFFFFFF)


def _rand_payload(rng: random.Random, max_size: int) -> bytes:
    # Choose among patterns and random mixes to cover a range of behaviors
    choice = rng.randrange(6)
    if choice == 0:
        # Pick one of predefined patterns, possibly slice it
        base = rng.choice(_DEF_PATTERNS)
        if not base:
            return base
        # Slice to a random sublength
        end = rng.randrange(0, min(len(base), max_size) + 1)
        return base[:end]
    elif choice == 1:
        # Random size with biased edge cases
        sizes = [0, 1, 2, 3, 15, 16, 31, 32, 255, 256, 1023, 1024, 2047, 2048, max_size]
        size = rng.choice([s for s in sizes if s <= max_size])
        return rng.randbytes(size)
    elif choice == 2:
        # Mixed segments: runs of zeros, 0xFF, ascending/descending, random
        parts: List[bytes] = []
        remaining = max_size
        while remaining > 0 and len(parts) < 8:
            kind = rng.randrange(5)
            seg_len = min(remaining, rng.randint(1, max(1, max_size // 4)))
            if kind == 0:
                parts.append(b"\x00" * seg_len)
            elif kind == 1:
                parts.append(b"\xff" * seg_len)
            elif kind == 2:
                # ascending pattern wrapped
                start = rng.randrange(256)
                parts.append(bytes(((start + i) & 0xFF) for i in range(seg_len)))
            elif kind == 3:
                # descending pattern wrapped
                start = rng.randrange(256)
                parts.append(bytes(((start - i) & 0xFF) for i in range(seg_len)))
            else:
                parts.append(rng.randbytes(seg_len))
            remaining -= seg_len
        return b"".join(parts)
    elif choice == 3:
        # Repetition of a short motif with occasional noise
        motif_len = rng.choice([1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 16, 32])
        motif = rng.randbytes(motif_len)
        reps = max_size // motif_len
        buf = motif * reps + motif[: (max_size - reps * motif_len)]
        # Flip a few random positions
        flips = min(8, len(buf))
        ba = bytearray(buf)
        for _ in range(flips):
            i = rng.randrange(len(ba))
            ba[i] ^= rng.randrange(256)
        return bytes(ba)
    elif choice == 4:
        # Structured blocks with sentinel bytes at edges
        size = rng.randint(0, max_size)
        if size == 0:
            return b""
        ba = bytearray(rng.randbytes(size))
        # Place notable bytes at interesting positions
        for pos in {0, size - 1, size // 2}:
            if size:
                ba[pos] = rng.choice([0x00, 0xFF, 0x7F, 0x80, 0x41])
        return bytes(ba)
    else:
        # Full 0..255 cycle repeated, cut to max_size
        base = (bytes(range(256)) * ((max_size // 256) + 1))[:max_size]
        # Optionally rotate
        rot = rng.randrange(256) if max_size > 0 else 0
        return base[rot:] + base[:rot]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide total payload size (for FUZZ_PARAM_STR) up to 4096
    max_total = 4096

    # Decide a buffer length biased toward small and boundary sizes
    size_choices = [0, 1, 2, 3, 7, 8, 15, 16, 31, 32, 63, 64, 255, 256, 511, 512, 1023, 1024, 2047, 2048, 3072, 4095, 4096]
    # Occasionally choose a random in range
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        payload_len = rng.choice(size_choices)
    else:
        payload_len = rng.randint(0, max_total)

    payload = _rand_payload(rng, payload_len)

    # Indices a,b used by the harness are computed modulo n+1 from two uint32s.
    # Provide values that often create edge subranges such as empty, full, prefix, suffix.
    n = len(payload)
    # Choose a and b in [0, n]
    a = rng.choice([0, n, n // 2, n // 3, (2 * n) // 3] + ([1, n - 1] if n >= 2 else [0])) if n > 0 else 0
    b = rng.choice([0, n, n // 2, n // 3, (2 * n) // 3] + ([1, n - 1] if n >= 2 else [0])) if n > 0 else 0

    # Convert to ri, rj such that ri % (n+1) == a, rj % (n+1) == b
    mod = (n + 1) if n >= 0 else 1
    # Pick random k to vary the higher bits
    ri = a + mod * rng.randrange(0, 17)
    rj = b + mod * rng.randrange(0, 17)

    # behavior for predicate overload: set bit 0 randomly
    behavior = rng.getrandbits(32)
    # Bias to sometimes stop (bit 0 set) when len>0; leave as random

    header = _pack_u32(ri) + _pack_u32(rj) + _pack_u32(behavior)

    # Concatenate header and payload. Harness will first consume the three u32
    # via FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int), then FUZZ_PARAM_STR reads the remaining bytes
    # as the buffer. Some fuzzers read FUZZ_PARAM_STR first; to still be useful,
    # we also append the header at the end in that case when payload is tiny.
    out = header + payload

    # Ensure we don't exceed 4096 bytes
    if len(out) > max_total:
        out = out[:max_total]

    return out
